# Ei

> Local-first AI memory layer for coding tools, with a persistent persona companion system on top.

Ei runs as a TUI (`bunx ei-tui`) or web app (ei.flare576.com). It ingests sessions from OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Pi, extracts facts/topics/people, and makes that memory available back to your coding tools via MCP and CLI context injection. Optionally, it hosts AI personas with persistent identity, heartbeats, and evolving traits.

## Setup

- [Quick Start](tui/README.md) — install, run, and pick your path (memory layer vs. persona companion)
- [Coding Tool Integrations](README.md#coding-tool-integrations) — enable session ingestion for OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Pi
- [MCP + CLI wiring](src/cli/README.md) — wire up MCP server and context injection so agents can read Ei memory

## For AI Assistants: Setting Up Ei

If a user asks you to set up Ei, these are the steps:

1. **Install Bun** (if not present): `curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash`
2. **Run Ei**: `bunx ei-tui` — no install needed, always current
3. **On first launch**: Ei auto-detects LLM providers from env vars (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, etc.). If a local LLM is running on port 1234, it's detected automatically.
4. **Enable coding tool integrations**: Open `/settings` in the TUI, set `opencode.integration: true` (and/or `claudeCode`, `cursor`, `codex`, `pi`) for the tools the user has installed.
5. **Wire up MCP**: Run `ei --install` to register the MCP server and install context injection hooks for all detected coding tools.
6. **Verify**: Run `ei mcp` — should list available memory query tools.

The default data path is `~/.local/share/ei`. No `EI_DATA_PATH` setup needed unless the user wants a custom location.
